articles.title: Bart Scott’s ruthless reminder about ‘dumb players’ turned analysts sends NFL fans into a frenzy
articles.summary: Former Baltimore Ravens linebacker Bart Scott might have ruffled the feathers of some of his colleagues with his recent admission about former players turned...
articles.body:
Former Baltimore Ravens linebacker Bart Scott might have ruffled the feathers of some of his colleagues with his recent admission about former players turned TV analysts.

Players pursuing a career in media after retirement is not an unknown route, and some of the greatest NFL stars have also done it. Tom Brady and T.J. Watt are two prime examples of NFL legends who moved into sports broadcasting after their careers.

With the rise of YouTube, many former players also use that as a platform to express their thoughts. However, Bart Scott does not agree to every former player's thoughts for a major reason.

Scott's take on former players turned analysts has fans in splits

Scott was one of the many former players who lost their jobs during the job cuts made by ESPN in July. He had been with the broadcaster for nine years, but was let go due to the corporate restructuring of talent. He had a show on ESPN Radio alongside Chris Carlin and also served as a studio analyst for SNY's New York Jets postgame show.

Despite his involvement in media, Scott believes not every former player on TV is qualified to offer takes on the game.

"You know and I know there's levels to this; every player that play in the league ain't smart, you had dumb players, right… Some couldn't coach their way out of a wet paper bag and we know, but they sound good, they can tap dance, they can present good. Half of them don't even have resumes. One thing I always say, 'You can say it, but can you show me how you did it.'" said Scott on The Pivot Podcast.

An X user reposted the clip, adding a split image of Dan Orlovsky and Emmanuel Acho at the end.

This led to a lot of reactions from fans, who stormed the comment section with their thoughts.

One fan said, "Screaming at the split image at the end," While another added, "orlovsky catching strays on the pivot is the best part of the whole network tbh."

Someone also stated, "I think I know who he talking about?!"

There were also those who did not agree with Scott's take on the topic. "This argument doesn't hold weight though, considering the best coaches typically are the bench players. Especially the backup QBs. Gary Kubiak, Kellen Moore, Kevin O'Connell.. all respected coaches who played way less on the field than Dan Orlovsky," the fan wrote.

A fan also opined, "BART is a dude that belongs on tv. He was funny without even trying on get up. Then he'd turned to the camera with a smirk like George Foreman used to."

articles.title: Don't blame Commanders' running backs for run game issues
articles.summary: The Commanders have struggled to run the ball consistently outside of Jayden Daniels. Don't blame the running backs.
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders ' offense under new coordinator David Blough has shown glimpses of greatness through three games this season. The season started frustratingly, as Washington failed to get anything going until the fourth quarter in a Week 1 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles .

In Week 2, the Commanders were back on the road at Dallas, and quarterback Jayden Daniels looked as electric as he did in 2024, putting Washington on the doorstep of a tie before dislocating his elbow at the end of the first half.

Marcus Mariota replaced Daniels and played well against Dallas. He appeared to throw a touchdown pass to Dyami Brown in the third quarter, but the officials ruled it incomplete. No one could believe it. From there, Washington's defense couldn't keep up with the Cowboys.

Last week, Mariota started against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. He was outstanding, completing 19 of 31 passes for 183 yards and three touchdowns. He took care of the football, watched as Washington's defense forced turnovers, and used his legs to seal the game in the fourth quarter. While the Commanders didn't put up huge numbers, they mostly did what they wanted through the air against Seattle's top-ranked defense.

Washington's offense has had its issues. Injuries have hurt them, including to Daniels, right guard Sam Cosmi, and left tackle Laremy Tunsil. Last week against Seattle, the Commanders featured a reshuffled offensive line, with recently signed Lucas Patrick at center. Those injuries have contributed to Washington's inability to run the ball. Amazingly, the Commanders are No. 8 in the NFL in rushing offense, averaging 132 yards per game. They are No. 17 in yards per attempt at 4.1.

However, those numbers are deceiving. Quarterback Jayden Daniels has 100 rushing yards and averages eight yards per attempt in his two games. Washington's three running backs who have played, Jacory Croskey-Merritt, Rachaad White, and Kaytron Allen, are averaging a combined 3.6 yards per attempt.

It's not quite fair to blame Washington's running backs, though.

According to Warren Sharp of Sharp Analysis , the Commanders' running backs have been hit at or behind the line of scrimmage on 53% of their runs — the third-highest total in the NFL. Interestingly, Sunday's Week 4 opponent, the Indianapolis Colts, rank second-highest.

That number tells you Washington's offensive line is allowing far too much penetration to opposing defenses. While Mariota can still run, he's much less dynamic than Daniels. Many believe Daniels will return in Week 5 against the New York Giants , which should help the running game.

In the meantime, perhaps the Commanders' running game can get going against the Colts in Week 4. Indianapolis ranks No. 29 in run defense, allowing over 141 yards per game.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Puka Nacua's Snap Count in Return From Injury for Rams vs. Eagles
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua reportedly won't be on a snap count when he returns to the lineup Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua reportedly won't be on a snap count when he returns to the lineup Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

"The Rams want to see Nacua's conditioning level once he's out on the field against the Eagles -- and that always could impact his snap count -- but they enter Sunday with no intention of limiting his snaps, according to sources," per Schefter.

"Sources told ESPN last week that Nacua was dealing with mainly a groin injury that was impacting his explosiveness," according to Schefter. The two-time Pro Bowler did not feel like he could play with the same explosiveness he had in the past, but the Rams viewed it as a short-term injury that they did not believe would require surgery."

Tom Pelissero of The Ringer previously reported on Saturday that it was determined that Nacua did not need surgery on the groin injury that kept him out of L.A.'s past two games, but he "may be on a stricter snap count than usual" this week.

Still, Pelissero noted that there is "optimism" Nacua will be able to "make an impact" on the field this weekend.

In Week 1, Nacua led the Rams with five receptions for 74 yards, but they fell 27-7 to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Coming out of that game, Rams head coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua had "a little bit of soreness" in his groin, and he went on to miss the team's win over the New York Giants in Week 2 and loss to the Denver Broncos in Week 3.

Nacua had been nursing a psoas injury during training camp, but McVay noted that the groin ailment was a separate issue.

In Nacua's absence, Davante Adams was clearly quarterback Matthew Stafford's top target in the passing game, as he went off for eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns against the Giants, and seven grabs for 137 yards against the Broncos.

While Adams is still a dangerous player and a potential future Hall of Famer, there is no question that Nacua is the Rams' WR1 when he is healthy and playing.

The 2023 fifth-round pick out of BYU is coming off a career season in 2025 that saw him lead the NFL with 129 receptions, while also recording 1,715 yards and 10 touchdowns.

Nacua was named a Pro Bowler for the second time and a First Team All-Pro for the first time as a result.

Even if he is at less than 100 percent and doesn't play his usual amount of snaps, having Nacua back in Week 4 should be huge for the Los Angeles offense.

Nacua is going to command defensive attention whenever he is on the field, so even if passes aren't going his way, he figures to open things up for Adams and the Rams' other wide receivers and tight ends.

Sunday's road game against the Eagles is a big one for the Rams since a loss would drop them to 1-3 on the season, which is something few would have expected out of the preseason favorite to win the Super Bowl.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Injury Update, New Rumors on Cowboys CB's Status & Snap Count After Steelers Trade
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who arrived in town after the Pittsburgh Steelers traded him on Wednesday, is set to make his debut Sunday at the Houston Texans after recovering from a back injury.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who arrived in town after the Pittsburgh Steelers traded him on Wednesday, is set to make his debut Sunday at the Houston Texans after recovering from a back injury .

NFL insider Jordan Schultz first reported on Saturday that Porter Jr. is expected to play, while ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday morning that Porter Jr. will be on a snap count:

Porter does not have an injury designation and Stephen Jones previously told reporters he believed the cornerback "will get snaps."

"We're just trying to take things day by day, and if everything looks good, then we should be out there," Porter said following his first Cowboys practice on Thursday, per ESPN's Todd Archer .

Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed optimism about Porter's chances, via Archer.

"We'd like him to play, but we'll see how the week goes. I think he's excited about the opportunity to maybe play, but we'll see how the rest of the week goes. But it was a good start today," Schottenheimer said.

Porter, a former Penn State star, was the No. 32 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft. He played his first three seasons with the Steelers, amassing 165 tackles (120 solo), 31 pass breakups and three interceptions over 47 games (41 starts).

Last year, opposing quarterbacks only completed 32-of-66 passes in his direction en route to a paltry 57.2 QB rating, per Pro Football Reference .

Porter entered this season on the final year of his rookie contract, and he and the Steelers worked toward a contract extension. However, one never materialized, leading to a months-long standoff.

Archer and ESPN's Brooke Pryor provided more information on Porter, who did not participate in any offseason activities leading into the regular season.

"The heart of the dispute was the guaranteed money within the contract's structure, sources told ESPN, and the sides never made meaningful progress on agreeing to terms despite talks as late as hours before kickoff of the Steelers' Week 1 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Steelers then stopped talks because they don't negotiate during the regular season as a longstanding organizational principle."

Porter hadn't played in the Steelers' first three games as he dealt with the aforementioned back issue plus conditioning concerns. He gave some insight to reporters (h/t Pryor) about the matter on Wednesday.

"It's both," Porter said. "My back has its moments where [there's] a flare-up here and there, and we're still just trying to get my conditioning down to just me being out there as much as possible."

The Steelers soon traded Porter to Dallas for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-rounder. Now he'll joins a pass defense that can use his services. The Cowboys have allowed the sixth-most passing yards per attempt ( 7.2 ) in the NFL. They've also given up seven passing touchdowns and no interceptions thus far.

Kickoff in Houston is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Sam LaPorta, Lions Failed Contract Talks Ahead of Free-Agency Decision
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta have ceased negotiations on a new contract, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions and tight end Sam LaPorta have ceased negotiations on a new contract, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

"Barring a significant breakthrough, LaPorta is set to be a free agent in 2027 and would become one of the top free agents regardless of position," Rapoport reported Sunday. "Detroit would also have the franchise tag available."

The NFL insider said the two sides made "a push on Friday and Saturday" to no avail.

The Lions didn't secure a long-term extension for edge-rusher Aidan Hutchinson until late October last year. A similar outcome with LaPorta is theoretically possible.

"The Lions continue to negotiate deals in-season and there is, at least, a chance they make another attempt at a deal that would make LaPorta one of the NFL's highest-paid tight ends," per Rapoport.

This may instead reflect the fact general manager Brad Holmes has to draw a line in the sand at some point with so many of Detroit's young stars getting pay raises around the same time.

The Lions have nine players earning at least $20 million annually, and quarterback Jared Goff is the only one from that group who wasn't drafted by the Lions. One downside of having a succession of strong draft classes is that a front office will need to hand out a lot of extensions within a short period of time.

Detroit would like to keep LaPorta around. The 2023 Pro Bowler has 14 catches for 144 yards and one touchdown through three games. He has recovered nicely from a herniated disc that ended his 2025 season and then a hip injury that jeopardized his status for the start of this year.

Tight end isn't a premium position, though, and LaPorta hasn't excelled on the field.

One could argue the 25-year-old is at least on the level of Tucker Kraft or Kyle Pitts, who got lucrative deals this summer, but he's not necessarily indispensible to an offense that includes Jahmyr Gibbs, Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams.

The franchise tag will be an option for the Lions to keep LaPorta around through 2027. In the absence of an agreement on a new multiyear contract, that's probably the likeliest outcome.

articles.title: Why Steelers Traded Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys Revealed in New NFL Rumors After Contract Standoff
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers reportedly traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys because of their refusal to include a second-year guarantee during contract discussions.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers reportedly traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys because of their refusal to include a second-year guarantee during contract discussions.

ESPN's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Pittsburgh offered the cornerback a contract that would have paid him an "acceptable" $28 million in average annual value. However, the team "held firm" on its usual stance that it would avoid injury guarantees after the first year of the deal even though it did give pass-rusher T.J. Watt such a second-year guarantee in the past.

"Declining to do so for Porter led to the contract impasse," Rapoport reported, adding the cornerback "wanted the security of a long-term contract rather than a large one-year payment" and "knew he would have been unlikely to play for Pittsburgh without a new contract."

Rapoport noted the Green Bay Packers and Cincinnati Bengals are also teams that typically take such a stance with second-year guarantees.

In addition to Watt, Steelers wide receiver DK Metcalf also has one, although that came along in a trade. And Watt is one of the best defensive players in the league and a foundational superstar with a Defensive Player of the Year and eight Pro Bowl nods on his resume, so some flexibility is understandable.

Porter, who was also dealing with a back injury in addition to the contract impasse, ultimately sat out training camp.

Pittsburgh traded him to the Cowboys for a 2027 sixth-round draft pick and a 2028 second-round draft pick in what Rapoport called its "only serious offer" even though the Detroit Lions were also suitors.

Dallas is 25th in the league in points allowed per game in the early going this season and could certainly use the help in the secondary. The NFC East team is also not wasting much time getting him on the field with the expectation he will play Sunday's game against the Houston Texans.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday the plan is for Porter to play "about 30 snaps or so, depending on the flow of the game."

When healthy, the 26-year-old can be one of the best cornerbacks in the league. In fact, he held opposing quarterbacks to a 57.2 passer rating and 48.5 completion percentage when targeted last season, per Pro Football Reference .

That type of coverage would provide an immediate boost for the Cowboys, who are looking to bounce back from their 1-2 start.

The 6-foot-2, 216-pound quarterback started 42 of 48 college games between Minnesota and Rutgers. His 2025 season was his best statistically, with 3,124 yards and 20 touchdown passes.There is also a personal story behind his unusual first name. Kaliakmanis is Greek American, and his father, Alex, chose Athan after seeing an icon of Saint Athanasius of Alexandria at a Greek Orthodox church in Perth Amboy, New Jersey. articles.title: Jerry Jones hints NFL could be thinking about embracing geographic rivalries
articles.summary: Since the Texans joined the NFL in 2002, they've faced the Cowboys only seven times.
articles.body:
Since the Texans joined the NFL in 2002, they've faced the Cowboys only seven times. The eighth meeting happens today.

During his Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he'd like to play the Texans more often. And he suggested the league is considering the possibility of embracing geographic rivalries between teams from opposing conferences.

"You can add that in the mix, and I'm not saying it's not in the mix ," Jones said. "It's just that other things come up and you have a different reason for the scheduling. We obviously have a rotation involved that is the best as far as fair, complete competition year-in, year-out, around the entire league. But it's certainly something that I would look at.

"And I wouldn't just narrow it down to Dallas and Houston. I'd look at the entire league, you saw a game on TV [Thursday] night between Cleveland and Pittsburgh. They're in the same division, but those kinds of proximities, those kinds of 'my town against your town, and who's the best town?' Which I think is a fundamental of our game of football. 'My town against your town. My school against your school.' That's a big part of it. It's hard to emulate anyplace but in the United States to get that rolling."

It would have been a great way to deal with the 17th game. Instead, the league added an interconference game tied to a rotation of divisions and the spot at which the team finished in the prior season. Perhaps the geographic rivalries could become a feature of an 18-game season. (Or the inevitable 19-game season.)

Beyond the Texans and the Cowboys, other no-brainer annual interconference rivalries would include the Jets and Giants, the Rams and Chargers, the 49ers and Raiders, the Ravens and Commanders, the Steelers and Eagles, the Buccaneers and Jaguars, the Titans and Falcons.

There wouldn't be 16 natural fits, so the league would have to identify one annual rival for each team if it ever adopts that approach. Packers and Chiefs. Bears and Colts (especially if the Bears move to Indiana). Lions and Browns. Broncos and Seahawks.

There would still be questions to answer. Who would the Bills' and Patriots' annual rivals be? Would the Vikings and Bengals become a geographic rivalry by default?

The Dolphins would perhaps fit with the Saints or Panthers. The Cardinals would be lost in the wilderness.

Still, the existence of a few forced rivalries would be more than offset by a cluster of annual games between teams linked by location. The league could even set the games for the same weekend every year, with a marketing slogan and special Nike uniforms.

And, yes, the more it could be turned into a moneymaker, the more likely it would be to happen.

Quarterback Blake Roskopf (Goodyear, Arizona/ Desert Edge High School) was officially honored as a 2027 Navy All-American by America's Navy and NBC Sports representatives during a live jersey presentation as part of the Road to the Dome tour.

Roskopf will play in the annual East vs. West matchup inside the Alamodome in San Antonio, Texas at 1 p.m. ET on Saturday, January 9, 2027, live on NBC and Peacock, which marks the twenty-seventh anniversary of the event.

The nationwide Road to the Dome tour will honor 100 Navy All-Americans with live and virtual jersey presentations.The series will be released weekly through social platforms across NBC Sports.

Roskopf was selected by the Navy All-American Bowl Selection Committee, comprised of the All-American Bowl, Andrew Ivins (247Sports), Brandon Huffman (Rivals), and NXGN. Navy All-Americans are eligible for the Navy All-American Bowl Player of the Year Award, Anthony Muñoz Lineman of the Year Award, Navy All-American Bowl Defensive Player of the Year Award, Navy All-American Bowl Man of the Year, and Navy All-American Bowl Game MVP Award.

As an NBC Sports-owned property, the All-American Bowl is part of a marquee lineup of elite events that includes the Olympics and Paralympics, the NBA, WNBA, Major League Baseball, Notre Dame Football, the Premier League, and primetime's #1 show for an unprecedented 15 consecutive years: Sunday Night Football . The All-American Bowl is annually the most-watched, most-talked about, and most-prestigious high school all-star event with more than four million unique television viewers and more than 25,000 fans in attendance. The history and tradition of the All-American Bowl is unparalleled, as it features: 665 draft picks; 110 Super Bowl champions; 300 Pro Bowl selections; and 18 Heisman finalists.
